rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for spatial or temporal distance, and it can mean “the farther one” when the comparison is clear.

example.english: This place is very far from downtown.
example.jyutping: ni1 dou6 lei4 si5 keoi1 hou2 jyun5

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken choice for a great distance in space or figurative extent.

example.english: It’s far to walk from here to the station.
example.jyutping: ni1 dou6 haang4 heoi3 ce1 zaam6 hou2 jyun5 wo3

rows.note: Use this instead of 好遠 when the great distance is in time rather than space.

example.english: It’s been far too long since I last saw you.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hou2 noi6 mou5 gin3 gwo3 nei5 laa3

rows.note: Use this before or after a comparative to mean that the difference is very large, as in being far richer.

example.english: Their salary is far higher than ours.
example.traditional: 佢份人工比我哋高好多。
example.jyutping: keoi5 fan6 jan4 gung1 bei2 ngo5 dei6 gou1 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this spoken comparative when you need to make clear which of two objects or places is farther away.

example.english: That shop is far away—it's farther than the other one.
example.traditional: 嗰間舖頭遠啲，行過去要十分鐘。
example.jyutping: go2 gaan1 pou3 tau4 jyun5 di1 haang4 gwo3 heoi3 jiu3 sap6 fan1 zung1

rows.note: Use this for a position or viewpoint at the extreme rather than near the middle, such as the far right politically.

example.english: Their political position is far too extreme.
example.traditional: 佢嘅政治立場太極端喇。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ge3 zing3 zi6 lap6 coeng4 taai3 gik6 dyun1 laa3
